To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a new method for TR-SAXS measurements of systems where the reaction process is initiated by removal of a substance was developed; 2) this method was used to investigate the self-association of insulin analogues; 3) the results show that this method can be applied in other systems where the reaction can be initiated by removing a substance or by other changes in experimental condition.

(i) a method is presented to study processes triggered by removal of species, (ii) the method is based on online HPLC facilitated buffer exchange and (iii) the method was applied to a system with long-acting insulin and phenol, where the removal of phenols triggers the self-association of insulin.
the presented method can be used to obtain TR-SAXS measurements of reactions initiated by removal of a species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods and applications of SAXS in structural biology.
developing methods to study complex biological systems using SAXS.
developing new experimental techniques to facilitate the analysis of complex systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this method can be used to study reactions triggered by buffer exchange.
this method is a useful tool for TR-SAXS studies of processes where a species is removed from the sample.
the method is suitable to study processes that can be initiated by removal of a species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can follow the kinetics of the self-association process by TR-SAXS and that the data are consistent with a model of self-association.
we have shown that TR-SAXS can be applied to study the self-association process for insulin analogues.
the removal of phenols from a mixture of insulin analogues and phenols triggers the self-association of long-acting insulins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TR-SAXS is an important tool for understanding the mechanisms behind biological processes in development and that the presented method can be applied in a wide variety of situations.
it is possible to follow the evolution of a system over time by using online buffer exchange and HPLC to trigger a process.
the method can be generally used for any system that is triggered by removal or addition of a species.
